title: Kotlin
subtitle: Concise, null-safe Kotlin 2 on the JVM, from a first program to data classes, sealed hierarchies, generics, coroutines and Java interoperability.
description: Kotlin is a statically typed language from JetBrains that compiles to Java bytecode (and also to native code, JavaScript and WebAssembly). It is the preferred language for Android, a popular choice for server-side development alongside Java, and the basis of Kotlin Multiplatform for sharing code between Android, iOS, desktop and the web. Its hallmarks are concise code, null safety checked by the compiler, and seamless use of every Java library.

This course is for anyone who can already write a small program with variables, decisions and loops, at the level of the [Start level of Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience; knowing Java helps but is not required. It goes from installing the compiler and a first program, through null safety, functions and lambdas, classes, data and sealed classes, collections and scope functions, to generics and variance, coroutines and structured concurrency, Java interoperability, Gradle and testing, ending with a complete small project.

To run the code, use the official [Kotlin Playground](https://play.kotlinlang.org/) in the browser, or install the compiler from the [Kotlin website](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/command-line.html) (or IntelliJ IDEA, which includes it) together with a JDK. Every complete program in these lessons was compiled with Kotlin 2.4 and run on JDK 21.
